title: Load a filled syringe into a syringe pump: flange in its slot, driver up to the plunger without pushing it
instruction: Load the filled syringe into the syringe pump. Lay it in the pump's cradle with the flange at the end of its barrel down in the flange slot, then slide the grey plunger driver along its track until it is up against the end of the plunger, without pushing the plunger in.
context: Loading a syringe pump is routine nursing work. Giving medications is a core duty of registered nurses (3.47 million in the US) and licensed practical nurses (667,000); O*NET: "Administer medications to patients and monitor patients for reactions or side effects" (29-1141.00). Drugs that need a slow, exact rate, in intensive care, neonatal units and on wards, go through syringe pumps, and each syringe is loaded by hand. Medfusion 3500 quick reference guide: "Make sure the flange on the syringe barrel is secure in the syringe barrel flange clip", then "gently advance the plunger driver toward the syringe plunger" until "it is flush". PMDA (Japan) Medical Safety Information No. 50 reports a flange not in the slit, where "the set drug volume will not be injected", and warns of siphoning when plunger and slider are not in contact. A driver that pushes the plunger in gives a dose nobody set. Done by: registered and licensed practical nurses.
setup: Positions in cm on the table, from the midpoint between the two arm bases: x forward (away from the arms), y to the robot's left. A white syringe pump, fixed, centred at x 33, its cradle running along y: a white plastic body 5 cm wide (along x) and 2.35 cm tall, from y -5.5 to 4.45, with two white plastic rods 1 cm across and 2.8 cm apart (centre to centre) along its top, which the barrel rests between with its axis 3.98 cm up; the flange slot, 3.5 mm wide and reaching 14 mm below the seated barrel's lowest line, with a rounded mouth (5 mm radius), centred at y 5.125; past it, from y 5.8 to 14, the driver's track, and on it the grey plastic plunger driver (4 cm wide, 2 cm long, 3 cm tall, with a black grip 12 by 6 mm on top) that slides along y and starts with its face at y 11.85, 3 cm from the plunger. The syringe, a stand-in for a 60 mL syringe: a clear plastic barrel 29.6 mm across and 100 mm long with a nose at one end and at the other a flange 40 by 50 mm and 2.5 mm thick; 75 g. In it, a white plastic plunger (a rubber stopper, an 8 mm rod and a 30 mm square thumb disc, 12 g), pulled back full. The syringe lies on two black plastic stands (2 by 1 cm, 2.6 cm tall) at x 25, its barrel's centre at y -20, flange toward the pump (left).
scoring: The syringe is in the cradle when its barrel's nose end rests on the rods (the axis there within 3 mm of the cradle's centre line sideways, 2.5 mm of its seated height and 5 mm of its seated place along the cradle) and the barrel is within 15 degrees of the cradle's line. It is seated when the axis is within 1 mm of its seat (sideways and up), level and square to the cradle within 1.5 degrees, and the flange's centre is within 0.8 mm of the slot's (it has 0.5 mm a side). The plunger is in the barrel when its stopper is within 1 mm of the axis and its rod within 5 degrees of it. The plunger ever pushed in more than 1 mm or drawn back more than 3 mm, the plunger out of the barrel, or the syringe not in the cradle: 0. In the cradle, not seated (flange out of its slot, syringe cocked): 0.2. Seated: 0.5. Seated, the driver's face within 5 mm short of the thumb disc: 0.75. Seated, the driver's face from 1 mm short of the disc to 0.2 mm into it (the contact's overlap in the simulator) and everything still (under 1 cm/s and 0.5 rad/s, the driver moving under 0.5 mm a step): 0.9, and 1.0 once that has held for 1 s (the trial ends there). A driver face more than 0.2 mm past the disc holds nothing and scores 0.5. The plunger's travel is tracked through the whole trial, so a push or a pull undone later still scores 0. Possible scores: 0, 0.2, 0.5, 0.75, 0.9, 1.0. To check a real trial: a side video for the flange in its slot, the driver at the thumb disc and the plunger never moving off its graduation.
reset_notes: Pull the driver back to its start, take the syringe out and lay it on its stands flange toward the pump, with the plunger pulled back full.
fidelity: Stand-in sizes for a 60 mL syringe. The barrel is 16 flat staves and rests on two rods, a simple cradle; a real pump also clamps the barrel, which is left out. The stopper slides with little friction (a real one needs a firm push to start), so the scorer allows 1 mm of plunger travel from the driver's contact. The flange slot's mouth is rounded like a clip's lead-in. The driver slides without its release lever. Roll about the barrel's axis isn't scored.
